title: Executive sponsor check-in cadence and quarterly recap email sequence
content:
Purpose:
This working template is for Customer Success Managers to run short, high-value executive sponsor check-ins and to deliver a concise customer-facing quarterly recap email sequence. The aim: protect renewal motion, highlight outcomes, surface risks early, and create a low-friction path for follow-up (decisions, budget conversations, pilot extensions).

Audience:
Primary: Executive sponsor (VP+/C-level) at customer. Secondary: Sponsor's right-hand (platform / infra lead), our Redwood account exec when appropriate.

Format & Cadence recommendations:
- Quarterly Sponsor Check-in: 20 minutes, video or huddle. A single-slide pre-read + 10-minute update + 8-minute discussion + 2-minute next steps.
- Monthly touchpoint (optional): 10-minute sync for high-touch accounts or pre-renewal quarters.
- Renewal runbook: start 90 days before renewal; increase cadence to biweekly with commercial lead.

One-page Executive Slide (single slide pre-read) — suggested sections (use minimal bullets):
1) Top-line outcomes (1 sentence): adoption, ROI signal (e.g., latency improvements / cost per inference), any production wins.
2) Health snapshot: green/amber/red with 3 short reasons.
3) Key metrics (last 90 days vs prior 90): tokens/day, avg p95 latency, success rate (4xx/5xx), cost per 1k tokens, model mix %.
4) Risk & mitigation: 1–2 bullets.
5) Asks & next steps: decisions requested, timeline, who owns it.

Agenda (20 min):
- 0:00–02:00 — Quick hello + objective for this check-in.
- 02:00–06:00 — Top-line outcomes and wins (1–2 customer stories).
- 06:00–12:00 — Health snapshot + metric highlights (show the one-pager).
- 12:00–18:00 — Risks, blockers, and proposed mitigations.
- 18:00–19:30 — Decisions / asks.
- 19:30–20:00 — Confirm next steps and owners.

Health definitions (use these consistently):
- Green: Service meeting SLOs, no active escalations, adoption trending up (>10% q/q).
- Amber: One operational or quality issue or adoption flat, mitigation plan in play.
- Red: SLA breach, exec escalation open, or renewal at risk.

Renewal signals to track (automated / weekly):
- Usage delta vs forecast (tokens/day, endpoints invoked).
- Feature adoption (routes using new features, e.g., streaming, reranking).
- Support volume/frequency (tickets per week and severity).
- Eval regressions: percentage of prompts with quality regressions flagged.
- Commercial indicators: PO status, finance asks, procurement timeline.

Escalation triggers (immediate notification to AE + CSM lead):
- Production downtime > 30 minutes affecting SLOs.
- Two or more P1/P2 incidents in last 30 days.
- Adoption drops >25% month-over-month.
- Customer expresses intent to pause or reduce committed capacity.

Sample talking points (concise, executive-facing):
- Opening: "Thanks for a minute — in the last quarter we reduced average generation latency by 18% for your primary endpoint and that cut CPU cost per inference by ~14%."
- Value highlight: "The new prefix cache trimmed repeated prompt cost and delivered a 22% improvement in throughput for your chat service during peak hours."
- Risk framing: "We see a recurring 4xx spike tied to a new ingest pipeline; proposed short-term mitigation is a routing fallback while your infra team finishes the fix."

Sample subject lines (quarterly recap emails):
- "Q1 recap: latency gains and renewal checklist for [Customer]"
- "[Customer] — executive recap & recommended next steps (Q1 2025)"
- "Quarterly outcome summary: cost savings & operational notes"

Email sequence (3-touch cadence — start 7 days after QBR meeting if follow-up required):
1) Day 0 (meeting day) — Immediate recap email (CS owner -> sponsor + cc AE): short thank-you, attach one-pager, list agreed next steps with owners + dates.
   - Key: subject: "Thanks — QBR Recap & Next Steps ( [Customer] )"
   - Body: 4–6 bullets: wins, metrics headline, decisions/asks, next meeting date.
2) Day 7 — Action reminder (if any open items): single sentence headline + 1–2 bullets on blockers; ask for availability for decision if needed.
3) Day 21 — Resolution check + renewal nudge (if renewal window < 120 days): summary of open items, commercial ask (PO status or approval timeline), suggest 15-min alignment call.

Sample Immediate Recap Email (short):
Subject: Thanks — QBR Recap & Next Steps ( [Customer] )
Hi [Sponsor name],
Thanks again for your time today. Attached is the one-slide recap. Quick highlights:
• Top result: p95 latency down 18% for main endpoint
• Adoption: active routes up 12% q/q
• Risk: transient 4xx spike on the ingestion pipeline — we proposed a routing fallback (CS: Marco, due 2025-03-05)
Agreed next steps:
1) Validate fallback with infra (Owner: [Infra lead]) — due 2025-03-05
2) Pilot dedicated capacity for peak hours (Owner: AE) — target decision by 2025-04-01
If helpful, we can set a 15-minute follow-up next week.
Best,
Aisha

Checklist to attach to email when renewal approaching (attach spreadsheet or summary bullets):
- Contract expiry date
- Current committed monthly spend vs actual monthly usage
- Open SOWs or pilots
- Procurement / legal contact names & timeline
- Commercial options (early renewal discount, capacity ramp options, flexible termination clauses)

Internal handoff template to AE (copy into CRM):
- Renewal window start / end dates
- Current health status and risk reasons
- Decision/ask and proposed commercial terms
- Key stakeholders and contact cadence

Operational notes for CSM to prep before the check-in:
- Pull last 90 days of tokens/day, 95th percentile latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens.
- One short customer success story with customer-provided quote if available.
- Confirm commercial timeline with AE.
- Confirm there are no unacknowledged incidents in last 30 days.

Templates: calendar invite & Slack nudge
- Calendar title: "Executive Sponsor QBR — 20m: [Customer] / Redwood"
- Calendar description: 1-sentence objective + attach one-pager + video link.
- Slack nudge (DM to sponsor): short note 1 day ahead, attach slide.

Open questions / TODOs (keep this section updated in the doc):
- Should we standardize the one-pager layout across all CSMs? (PRO: consistent measurement; CON: less room for account nuance)
- Which customer metrics are required vs optional on the slide? Suggested required: tokens/day, p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, renewal date.
- Automation: can we generate the slide from our metrics warehouse (dashboard export) to reduce manual work? Ticket: JIRA:CS-4821.

Notes on tone & positioning for execs:
- Be concise. Execs read one-sentence outcomes; use numbers.
- Focus on business impact, not implementation detail unless asked.
- State asks clearly (decision needed, timeline, owner).

Appendix: quick examples of metric phrasing for one-pager
- "Tokens/day: 2.1M (▲ 12% q/q)"
- "p95 latency: 420ms (▼ 18% q/q)"
- "Error rate (4xx/5xx): 0.7% (stable)"
- "Cost per 1k tokens: $0.42 (▼ 14% after caching)"

Version history & notes:
- 2025-02-18 — initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2025-02-20 — added escalation triggers and renewal checklist (Marco A.)
- 2025-02-22 — updated sample email tones and metrics list (Samantha L.)

This is a working doc. Please copy and tailor each section for the customer before sending.
